Ransomware Attack Disrupts Construction Materials Sector in Cyprus

A major ransomware attack has disrupted operations across Cyprus’s construction materials industry, with Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd among several companies reporting significant IT system outages. The incident, which began late Monday evening, has crippled production and distribution channels, causing delivery delays and raising concerns over project timelines throughout the sector.

According to statements from affected firms and industry sources, the cyber attack targeted central IT systems, encrypting critical data and rendering key software inoperable. Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd confirmed it is “currently investigating and working to restore services as quickly as possible,” while urging customers to expect delays in orders and communication.

The Cyprus Association of Construction Materials Manufacturers said at least four major firms have reported “widespread operational disruptions” and that “the scale of this attack is unprecedented for our sector.” Local analysts estimate that daily production capacity across the industry may be down by as much as 40% as a result of the incident.

“We are seeing supply chain interruptions at a critical time for the industry, with many projects relying on just-in-time delivery of materials,” said Andreas Christou, an independent supply chain consultant based in Nicosia. “If the outage continues, construction schedules could be pushed back, impacting both private and public works.”

Employees at affected companies have been instructed not to use their computers until systems can be secured, according to a trade union representative. “Our members are concerned about the safety of their data and their ability to work,” said Maria Papadopoulou of the Building Materials Workers Union.

As of Tuesday afternoon, no group has claimed responsibility for the attack and it is unclear whether a ransom demand has been made. The affected companies have notified the Cyprus Police Cybercrime Unit, which is assisting with the investigation.

Industry insiders warn that the full impact on the construction supply chain will depend on how quickly systems can be restored. For now, the sector faces ongoing uncertainty as the situation continues to unfold.
